issues.explanation: firebase/php-jwt is added to composer.json, but composer.lock is not updated anywhere in the change. If the project tracks the lock (Laravel apps normally do), composer install in CI/deploy will not install the package and every totem endpoint will fail with a missing Firebase\JWT\JWT class; update the lock or confirm it is untracked.

The single-use guard updates the preset only by id and login_code_consumed_at. On SQLite, where lockForUpdate is a no-op, a concurrent totem:pairing-code run can replace login_code and clear consumed_at between the SELECT and this UPDATE, so a code that was just regenerated away can still pair. Include ->where('login_code', $code) (and ideally the active/expiry predicates) in the conditional update.

The optional-origin test first asserts allowed_origins is empty, so it fails on a developer .env that sets TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN, and it only re-requires config/cors.php instead of exercising the middleware for that origin. Pin TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN empty in phpunit.xml and assert a real preflight for the configured origin.

RateLimiter::clear('totem-auth') passes the limiter name, but clear() expects a concrete cache key (limiter keys are hashed), so the line is a no-op and does not reset the throttle between tests as intended.

fake()->unique() is scoped to one Faker/factory instance, so independently constructed TotemPreset factories can generate the same 6-digit code and hit the unique index. The task asks for a unique ready-to-use code; generate with random_int and retry on collision (or accept the rare failure explicitly).

The zero-padding test relies on 30 random draws and only observes the final length; assert the padding behavior deterministically (e.g. by injecting/seeding the generator) rather than relying on probability.

review.summary: This change implements the totem BFF end to end: the totem/preset schema, models and factories, the pairing command and actions, HS256 JWTs with the totem.auth middleware, the three scoped endpoints reusing IssueTicket, throttles, CORS, docs and a broad Pest suite. It is well structured and thoroughly tested; the main review items are the un-updated composer.lock, a narrow SQLite race in the conditional pairing-code consumption, and a few test-quality nits.
